label: Advanced Item API
title: Advanced Item API
bodyHtml:
When to use this page

The basic Item API page uses vanilla ItemInfo to mimic the base game. Advanced items can use CustomItemInfo, which includes normal ItemInfo fields, vanilla LiquidItemInfo fields, and CUCoreLib-only fields like Container, Battery, Light, Tool, Gun, WornSprite, MultiWornSprites, VisualOffset, WornSpriteOffset, MultiWornSpriteOffsets, LiquidMask, LiquidMaskAnimationId, SpriteScaleDimensions, DropPool, SpawnFrequency, WorldSpawnPerChunk, and CustomData.

Why is the mod doing it this way? Traditonally, the game sets these settings via the Unity prefab editor, and as such does not appear in the game's default item code.

// Replace new ItemInfo{ ... } with 
      new CustomItemInfo{ ... }

Modded-only fields

CustomItemInfo keeps vanilla fields like fullName, category, weight, tags, and useAction. It also exposes vanilla liquid-container fields like capacity, defaultContents, and autoFill. The fields below are CUCoreLib-only data. The base game does not know about them unless CUCoreLib reads them and applies the matching runtime behavior.

Field Type What CUCoreLib uses it for
IDstringFilled by ItemRegistry.Register from the separate ID argument. You normally do not set this yourself.
IconSpriteInventory/world sprite used by custom templates and cached under the item ID. Passing the sprite as the third register argument sets this for you.
WornSpriteSpriteOptional sprite applied while a wearable custom item is worn, then restored to Icon when dropped.
MultiWornSpritesDictionary<string, Sprite>Optional extra worn sprites keyed by vanilla limb name. CUCoreLib maps these onto the game's secondary wearable sprite arrays, so one wearable can draw on multiple limbs while equipped.
VisualOffsetVector2Optional local-space offset applied only while the item is held in a hand slot.
WornSpriteOffsetVector2Optional local-space offset applied to the worn item sprite after vanilla attaches it to desiredWearLimb.
WearableSortingOrderint?Optional worn-renderer sorting order override. When set, CUCoreLib applies that exact order to the main worn sprite and any MultiWornSprites; higher values draw on top of lower values.
MultiWornSpriteOffsetsDictionary<string, Vector2>Optional per-limb local offsets for entries in MultiWornSprites. Use matching limb keys, or fill it through SetMultiWornSpriteOffset(...).
LiquidMaskSpriteOptional liquid-fill overlay mask for custom WaterContainerItem containers. Use a white or neutral grayscale sprite with transparency shaping the visible fill area so the game can tint it to the current liquid color.
LiquidMaskAnimationIdstringOptional registered frame-animation ID for the liquid-fill mask. CUCoreLib assigns its first frame to vanilla fillSprite, then animates the generated fill renderer. Leave it empty to keep LiquidMask static.
SpriteScalefloatScale applied to the generated runtime template. Keep this near 1f unless your art was made at a different size.
InventoryIconScalefloatExtra multiplier applied only to the inventory icon UI size after the normal sprite scale has been resolved. Leave it at 1f unless you want the inventory icon smaller or larger than the in-world sprite.
SpriteScaleDimensionsSpriteScaleDimensionsScales the sprite toward a target pixel size like (14f, 14f). Add true as the third tuple value to stop once either axis reaches the requested size instead of forcing both axes to meet it.
DropPoolDropPool?Optional fixed loot-source flags such as DropPool.Corpse, DropPool.MedicalCrate, DropPool.AllTraders, DropPool.DropCapsule, or DropPool.CapsuleContainer. Leave it null to use category fallback.
SpawnFrequencyintPooled spawn weight. 0 means no pooled injection, 1 is the normal default, higher values make the item more common in category fallback or fixed DropPool sources.
WorldSpawnPerChunkfloat?Optional loose worldgen spawn density per chunk. Set it when the item should appear directly in the world after vanilla loot generation. This direct world-spawn count does not use SpawnFrequency.
ContainerContainerPropertiesAdds/configures a vanilla Container component on spawned items.
BatteryBatteryPropertiesAdds/configures a vanilla BatteryItem component on spawned items.
LightLightPropertiesAdds/configures a Light2D emitter and optionally wires it to vanilla LightItem behavior.
BandageBandagePropertiesInstalls a vanilla-style BandageMinigame limb action and applies limb healing, pain reduction, and bandage slow values.
SyringeSyringePropertiesAdds syringe-style liquid injection behavior through WaterContainerItem and SyringeMinigame.
ToolToolPropertiesBuilds a vanilla AttackInfo and calls Body.Attack for melee-style tools or weapons.
GunGunPropertiesConfigures GunScript behavior.
SpawnComponentsList<string>Backing list of runtime-resolvable MonoBehaviour type names CUCoreLib adds to the spawned item GameObject the first time the item appears. For plugin-defined scripts, prefer AddSpawnComponent<T>() so you do not have to hand-write the assembly-qualified name.
CustomDataDictionary<string, object>Inline defaults for mod-owned per-item custom state. CUCoreLib copies them onto each spawned item instance so your mod can read or mutate them later with ItemRegistry.GetCustomData<T> and ItemRegistry.SetCustomData.

LiquidItemInfo fields

Use these direct fields for normal liquid containers like bottles, cans, canteens, pouches, and drinkable items. Use SyringeProperties only when you want the syringe minigame and injection action.

If you want the container to render a vanilla-style colored fill overlay, pair those fields with LiquidMask on CustomItemInfo. The mask should usually be white or neutral grayscale, with transparency defining where the liquid can appear. To animate that mask, register frames first and set LiquidMaskAnimationId; the generated fill overlay uses the same timing as the rest of CUCoreLib's sprite animation system.

FieldTypeWhat it does
capacityfloatMaximum liquid capacity in mL.
defaultContentsList<LiquidStack>Liquids added to freshly spawned items.
autoFillboolWhether a loose item can fill itself from world liquid tiles when it has space.

ContainerProperties

FieldTypeWhat it does
CapacityfloatMaximum total held weight for the vanilla Container.
MaxWeightPerItemfloatMaximum weight any one contained item may have.
EncumbranceReductionfloatMultiplier for how much contained weight counts against the player. 1f is normal; 0.5f feels half as heavy.
ItemsVisibleboolControls the vanilla Container.itemsVisible flag. When true, contained item sprites remain visible inside the container.
TagRestrictionstring[]Optional whitelist of item tags accepted by the container. Leave empty to allow any tag.

BatteryProperties

FieldTypeWhat it does
StartChargefloatStarting charge amount for fresh spawned items. Values from 0f to 1f are treated as a percentage of the preset max charge. Higher values are treated as absolute charge. Leave it below zero to spawn with a full preset-sized battery.
PresetBatteryItem.BatteryPresetVanilla preset for accepted battery size: Small, Medium, or Large.
SpawnWithBatteryboolIf true, fresh items start with the preset-sized vanilla battery already loaded. If false, the item starts empty.

BandageProperties

FieldTypeWhat it does
EffectivenessfloatDivisor for minigame use amount. Higher values make the item last longer.
SkinHealAmountfloatSkin healing applied per use amount.
BandageSlowAmountfloatBleeding slowdown applied per use amount.
PainReductionfloatPain removed per use amount.
BoneHealTimerReductionfloatBroken-bone recovery timer reduction per use amount.
DislocationTimerReductionfloatDislocation timer reduction per use amount.
MinigameColorColorColor passed into the vanilla bandage minigame.
CreateWrapSpriteboolIf true, CUCoreLib creates a temporary limb wrap sprite when used.
WrapSpritePathstringResource path for the temporary wrap sprite.
WrapSpriteColorColorTint for the temporary wrap sprite.

SyringeProperties

This is for syringe-style limb injection, not general bottle/canteen liquid storage.

FieldTypeWhat it does
CapacityfloatMaximum liquid capacity in mL.
AutoFillboolWhether the added WaterContainerItem auto-fills when supported by vanilla behavior.
AmountPerFullUsefloatLiquid amount injected when the minigame multiplier is 1f.
UseAverageColorboolIf true, the minigame color comes from the contained liquid average.
MinigameColorColorFallback minigame color when UseAverageColor is false.
DefaultContentsList<LiquidStack>Liquids added to fresh spawned items.

ToolProperties

FieldTypeWhat it does
DamagefloatDamage against animals or living targets.
StructuralDamagefloatDamage against blocks, buildings, and non-animal structures.
AttackCooldownMultiplierfloatMultiplier applied to vanilla attack cooldown after hitting animals.
DistancefloatRaycast reach for the attack.
KnockBackfloatImpulse applied through vanilla attack knockback.
CooldownfloatBase attack cooldown.
AttackAnimationstringResource name for the swing animation prefab, usually SwingAnim.
StaminaUsefloatStamina spent when swinging.
PiercingboolIf true, vanilla attack raycasts can continue through hits.
SwingSoundsstring[]Sound IDs randomly chosen when swinging.
VolumefloatSwing sound volume.
RotateAmountfloatVisual attack rotation amount.
PhysicalSwingboolIf true, vanilla arm power, exertion, and physical swing effects apply.
DoAttackAnimationboolIf true, vanilla arms swing animation plays.
MetalMoreDamageboolIf true, vanilla metallic target bonus damage applies.
ConditionLossOnHitfloatItem condition subtracted after a successful hit.

LightProperties

FieldTypeWhat it does
IntensityfloatBrightness of the generated Light2D.
ColorColorLight tint. Defaults to white.
FalloffIntensityfloatRadial falloff, including for point/cone lights: 0f is sharp and 1f is soft. For cone-edge softness, set PointLightInnerAngle below PointLightOuterAngle. Defaults to 0.5f.
PointLightOuterRadiusfloatOuter radius for point lights.
PointLightInnerRadiusfloatInner radius for point lights.
PointLightOuterAnglefloatOuter cone angle for point lights. Defaults to 360f.
PointLightInnerAnglefloatInner cone angle for point lights. Defaults to 360f.
LightTypeCustomLightTypeCUCoreLib light type mapped internally to URP Light2D.LightType. Use CustomLightType.Point for lantern-style item light.
RotationfloatLocal Z-axis rotation in degrees. Use this to aim a cone-shaped point light.
OffsetVector2Local offset for the light object relative to the item.
AddLightItemboolIf true, CUCoreLib wires the light through vanilla LightItem so container/on-off behavior can apply.
 
ItemRegistry.Register(
    "SomeSlightlyMoreAdvancedItem",
    new CustomItemInfo
    {
        fullName = "someName",
        // ... and other ItemInfo fields...

          // Cool CUCoreLib-only fields!
          DropPool = DropPool.Corpse | DropPool.MedicalCrate | DropPool.AllTraders,
          SpawnFrequency = 0,
          WorldSpawnPerChunk = 0.02f,
          SpriteScale = 1f,
          CustomData =
          {
            ["family"] = "utility-bag"
        } 
        // etc...
    },
    AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.someSweetPixelArt.png")
);

Bandages

This is a bit different then the decompiled code. BandageProperties starts a BandageMinigame, converts the minigame angle into a use amount, reduces item condition, then adds limb healing and bleeding slowdown values.

ItemRegistry.Register(
    "clothpatch",
    new CustomItemInfo
    {
        fullName = "Cloth patch",
        description = "A small patch of clean cloth.",
        category = "medical",
        tags = "medicine,dressing,cangetwet",
        weight = 0.05f,
        value = 3,
        rec = new Recognition(3),
        Bandage = new BandageProperties
        {
            Effectiveness = 8f,
            SkinHealAmount = 8f,
            BandageSlowAmount = 18f,
            PainReduction = 40f,
            BoneHealTimerReduction = 5f,
            DislocationTimerReduction = 5f,
            MinigameColor = new Color(0.9f, 0.9f, 0.9f)
        },
        SpawnFrequency = 1
    },
    AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.clothpatch.png")
);

Syringes

SyringeProperties makes the item behave like a liquid syringe: CUCoreLib adds WaterContainerItem, starts SyringeMinigame, then calls wat.Inject(limb, amount) using the minigame multiplier.

ItemRegistry.Register(
    "reliefinjector",
    new CustomItemInfo
    {
        fullName = "Relief injector",
        description = "A small injector prefilled with relief cream.",
        category = "medicine",
        tags = "medicine",
        slotRotation = -45f,
        destroyAtZeroCondition = false,
        combineable = true,
        scaleWeightWithCondition = true,
        weight = 0.25f,
        value = 8,
        rec = new Recognition(5),
        Syringe = new SyringeProperties
        {
            Capacity = 100f,
            AmountPerFullUse = 100f,
            AutoFill = false,
            // Not sure what this is? Read the next page for liquid documentation.
            DefaultContents =
            {
                new LiquidStack("reliefcream", 100f)
            }
        },
        SpawnFrequency = 1
    },
    AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.reliefinjector.png")
);

The liquid decides what injection actually does. WaterContainerItem.Inject drains the liquid stack and calls onInject when that liquid is injectable, falling back to onHealthUse for older registrations.

You'll learn more about liquids and their use on the Liquids page.

Containers

Containers are runtime components, not just item stats. CUCoreLib's container module adds or configures a vanilla Container component when the item starts.

Capacity maps to the container's maximum held weight. MaxWeightPerItem limits individual items. EncumbranceReduction maps to the vanilla encumbrance multiplier: 1f means normal weight, 0.5f means the contents feel half as heavy.

ItemRegistry.Register(
    "cinderstalkbag",
    new CustomItemInfo
    {
        fullName = "Cinderstalk Bag",
        description = "A compact all-natural bag. Who says plants can't be stylish?",
        category = "custom",
        weight = 1.2f,
        value = 18,
        tags = "cangetwet",
        rec = new Recognition(6),
        Container = new ContainerProperties
        {
            Capacity = 5f,
            MaxWeightPerItem = 2f,
            EncumbranceReduction = 0.65f
        },
        SpawnFrequency = 1
    },
    AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.cinderstalk-bag.png")
);

Battery-powered items

Battery-powered tools use the vanilla BatteryItem component. CUCoreLib's battery module adds one, chooses the vanilla battery size from Preset, and uses StartCharge only for the initial fill amount. Use values from 0f to 1f when you want a percentage of the preset size, or values above 1f when you want an absolute charge amount. Use this when the item itself stores charge or accepts battery behavior; use vanilla BatteryInfo when you are registering an actual battery item.

Battery items automatically gain BatteryDecay, so you usually just set decayMinutes to control how quickly charge drains.

ItemRegistry.Register(
    "portablelamp",
    new CustomItemInfo
    {
        fullName = "Portable lamp",
        description = "A battery-fed lamp for the fuzzy cave explorer.",
        category = "utility",
        tags = "belttool",
        usable = true,
        value = 22,
        weight = 0.8f,
        rec = new Recognition(5),
        decayMinutes = 180f,
        Battery = new BatteryProperties
        {
            StartCharge = 35f,
            Preset = BatteryItem.BatteryPreset.Medium
        },
        Light = new LightProperties
        {
            Intensity = 0.75f,
            Color = Color.white,
            FalloffIntensity = 0.5f,
            PointLightOuterRadius = 7.5f,
            PointLightInnerRadius = 0f,
            PointLightOuterAngle = 360f,
            PointLightInnerAngle = 360f,
            LightType = CustomLightType.Point,
            Rotation = 0f,
            Offset = Vector2.zero
        },
        SpawnFrequency = 1
    },
    AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.portablelamp.png")
);

Non-gun weapons

For melee tools and small weapons, ToolProperties builds a vanilla AttackInfo and calls Body.Attack. This gives custom tools the same swing, raycast, hit sound, cooldown, damage-number, and block-damage path used by vanilla tools.

ItemRegistry.Register("glassshiv", new CustomItemInfo
{
    fullName = "Glass shiv",
    description = "A sharpened piece of glass wrapped in cloth.",
    category = "weapon",
    tags = "tool,cangetwet,cutting",
    weight = 0.25f,
    value = 4,
    rec = new Recognition(3),
    Tool = new ToolProperties
    {
        Damage = 22f,
        StructuralDamage = 8f,
        AttackCooldownMultiplier = 0.7f,
        Distance = 4.6f,
        KnockBack = 120f,
        Cooldown = 0.28f,
        StaminaUse = 0.35f,
        Piercing = true,
        ConditionLossOnHit = 0.08f
    }
}, AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.glassshiv.png"), 1);

Equippables

Wearables are regular items with wearable fields set. wearSlotId is the save/load and replacement key. desiredWearLimb points the primary visual/armor behavior at a body region, while wearableArmor and wearableIsolation affect protection and temperature. Use VisualOffset when you want the held hand sprite moved without changing the worn sprite, use MultiWornSprites when the same wearable should also draw extra pieces on other limbs, and set WearableSortingOrder when you need that whole wearable stack to use a higher or lower draw priority than other equipment.

If a wearable needs a custom script, use the same item-side AddSpawnComponent<T>() helper described below. There is no separate wearable-only script hook.

 ItemRegistry.Register(
     "fieldpack",
     new CustomItemInfo
     {
         fullName = "Field Pack",
         description = "A versatile pack for carrying supplies.",
         category = "tool",
         wearable = true,
         wearableCanBeHeld = true,
         desiredWearLimb = "UpTorso",
         wearSlotId = "back",
         wearableArmor = 0.18f,
         wearableIsolation = 0.08f,
         wearableHitDurabilityLossMultiplier = 0.7f,
         weight = 1.1f,
         value = 14,
         tags = "cangetwet",
         rec = new Recognition(4),
         WornSprite = AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.fieldpack-worn.png"),
         WornSpriteOffset = new Vector2(0f, -0.04f),
         VisualOffset = new Vector2(0f, -0.02f),
         WearableSortingOrder = 206,
         MultiWornSprites = new Dictionary
         {
             ["DownTorso"] = AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.fieldpack-bedroll.png"),
             ["HandB"] = AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.fieldpack-strap.png")
         },
         Container = new ContainerProperties
         {
             Capacity = 8f,
             MaxWeightPerItem = 3f,
             EncumbranceReduction = 0.5f
         },
         SpawnFrequency = 1
     }
     .SetMultiWornSpriteOffset(new Vector2(0f, -0.02f), AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.fieldpack-bedroll.png"))
     .SetMultiWornSpriteOffset("HandB", new Vector2(-0.01f, 0.01f)),
     AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.fieldpack.png")
 );

In this example, we combined the container tag, a primary WornSprite, and two MultiWornSprites entries to make one backpack draw across multiple limbs while still behaving like a normal wearable container.

A lot of more unique items such as this can be made with combinations of tags. Give it a try!

Targeting specific loot sources

Leave DropPool unset when the item should follow its broad category like vanilla. Set DropPool when the item should target explicit sources instead, such as corpses, one crate type, trader species, or capsules.

ItemRegistry.Register(
    "fieldbandagekit",
    new CustomItemInfo
    {
        fullName = "Field bandage kit",
        description = "A compact med kit meant for emergency caches and corpses.",
        category = "medical",
        tags = "medicine,dressing,cangetwet",
        weight = 0.25f,
        value = 12,
        DropPool = DropPool.Corpse | DropPool.MedicalCrate | DropPool.AllTraders,
        SpawnFrequency = 2,
        WorldSpawnPerChunk = 0.02f
    },
    AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.fieldbandagekit.png")
);

In that example, the item no longer relies on category fallback for pooled sources. It instead uses the explicit DropPool flags, while direct loose worldgen counts come from WorldSpawnPerChunk.

Decay bit flags

decayInfo is a byte, but it represents bit flags from ItemInfo.DecayType. Combine flags with bitwise OR (|). The enums are: NoDecayWithoutContainerItem (1), NoDecayWhenNotWorn (2), NoDecayWhenStill (4), and BatteryDecay (16).

decayMinutes = 240f,
decayInfo = (byte)(
    ItemInfo.DecayType.NoDecayWhenNotWorn | ItemInfo.DecayType.NoDecayWhenStill
);

BatteryDecay (16) changes decay from normal item condition loss into battery drain. Use it for battery-powered items that should consume charge over time instead of rotting or breaking down normally.

Note: The item still needs decayMinutes for decay speed.

SpawnComponents type names

!! Legacy !! Prefer custom item scripts, in the next page.

For plugin-authored item scripts, AddSpawnComponent<T>() exists. It stores the runtime-resolvable assembly-qualified name for you, so you do not have to hand-write Type.GetType(...) strings.

ItemRegistry.Register(
    "ToggleBlade",
    new CustomItemInfo
    {
        fullName = "Toggle blade",
        category = "weapon"
    }
    .AddSpawnComponent<ToggleBladeScript>(),
    icon
);

SpawnComponents remains the backing list, so you can still fill it manually for uncommon reflection-driven cases. When you do, use the full type name plus the assembly name without the .dll extension. Example: "TestModd.ToggleBladeScript, TestModd".

Custom data

CustomData is for your own mod's item-side custom state defaults: tuning values, upgrade tiers, internal labels, or small constants you want to keep near the registration. CUCoreLib copies those values onto each spawned item instance so one item can change without rewriting every other item of the same type.

ItemRegistry.Register(
    "laserdrill",
    new CustomItemInfo
    {
        fullName = "Laser drill",
        category = "tool",
        CustomData =
        {
            ["beamRange"] = 8f,
            ["warmupSeconds"] = 0.35f,
            ["upgradeFamily"] = "laserdrill"
        }
    },
    AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.laserdrill.png")
);

Retrieve it from the item with ItemRegistry.GetCustomData. The generic type is intentional: the dictionary stores object, so callers should ask for the type they expect.

float beamRange = ItemRegistry.GetCustomData(item, "beamRange", 4f);
Logger.LogInfo($"Laser drill range: {beamRange}");

Consider adding a function to encapsulate the retrieval logic.

If the data changes per spawned item, update it through ItemRegistry.SetCustomData rather than mutating the shared registered definition. Tile CustomData still remains registration metadata.

Field Type What it does Capacity float Maximum liquid capacity in mL. AutoFill bool Whether the added WaterContainerItem auto-fills when supported by vanilla behavior. AmountPerFullUse float Liquid amount injected when the minigame multiplier is 1f . UseAverageColor bool If true, the minigame color comes from the contained liquid average. MinigameColor Color Fallback minigame color when UseAverageColor is false. DefaultContents List<LiquidStack> Liquids added to fresh spawned items. ToolProperties Field Type What it does Damage float Damage against animals or living targets. StructuralDamage float Damage against blocks, buildings, and non-animal structures. AttackCooldownMultiplier float Multiplier applied to vanilla attack cooldown after hitting animals. Distance float Raycast reach for the attack. KnockBack float Impulse applied through vanilla attack knockback. Cooldown float Base attack cooldown. AttackAnimation string Resource name for the swing animation prefab, usually SwingAnim . StaminaUse float Stamina spent when swinging. Piercing bool If true, vanilla attack raycasts can continue through hits. SwingSounds string[] Sound IDs randomly chosen when swinging. Volume float Swing sound volume. RotateAmount float Visual attack rotation amount. PhysicalSwing bool If true, vanilla arm power, exertion, and physical swing effects apply. DoAttackAnimation bool If true, vanilla arms swing animation plays. MetalMoreDamage bool If true, vanilla metallic target bonus damage applies. ConditionLossOnHit float Item condition subtracted after a successful hit. LightProperties Field Type What it does Intensity float Brightness of the generated Light2D . Color Color Light tint. Defaults to white. FalloffIntensity float Radial falloff, including for point/cone lights: 0f is sharp and 1f is soft. For cone-edge softness, set PointLightInnerAngle below PointLightOuterAngle . Defaults to 0.5f . PointLightOuterRadius float Outer radius for point lights. PointLightInnerRadius float Inner radius for point lights. PointLightOuterAngle float Outer cone angle for point lights. Defaults to 360f . PointLightInnerAngle float Inner cone angle for point lights. Defaults to 360f . LightType CustomLightType CUCoreLib light type mapped internally to URP Light2D.LightType . Use CustomLightType.Point for lantern-style item light. Rotation float Local Z-axis rotation in degrees. Use this to aim a cone-shaped point light. Offset Vector2 Local offset for the light object relative to the item. AddLightItem bool If true, CUCoreLib wires the light through vanilla LightItem so container/on-off behavior can apply. ItemRegistry.Register( "SomeSlightlyMoreAdvancedItem", new CustomItemInfo { fullName = "someName", // ... and other ItemInfo fields... // Cool CUCoreLib-only fields! DropPool = DropPool.Corpse | DropPool.MedicalCrate | DropPool.AllTraders, SpawnFrequency = 0, WorldSpawnPerChunk = 0.02f, SpriteScale = 1f, CustomData = { ["family"] = "utility-bag" } // etc... }, AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.someSweetPixelArt.png") ); Bandages This is a bit different then the decompiled code. BandageProperties starts a BandageMinigame , converts the minigame angle into a use amount, reduces item condition, then adds limb healing and bleeding slowdown values. ItemRegistry.Register( "clothpatch", new CustomItemInfo { fullName = "Cloth patch", description = "A small patch of clean cloth.", category = "medical", tags = "medicine,dressing,cangetwet", weight = 0.05f, value = 3, rec = new Recognition(3), Bandage = new BandageProperties { Effectiveness = 8f, SkinHealAmount = 8f, BandageSlowAmount = 18f, PainReduction = 40f, BoneHealTimerReduction = 5f, DislocationTimerReduction = 5f, MinigameColor = new Color(0.9f, 0.9f, 0.9f) }, SpawnFrequency = 1 }, AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.clothpatch.png") ); Syringes SyringeProperties makes the item behave like a liquid syringe: CUCoreLib adds WaterContainerItem , starts SyringeMinigame , then calls wat.Inject(limb, amount) using the minigame multiplier. ItemRegistry.Register( "reliefinjector", new CustomItemInfo { fullName = "Relief injector", description = "A small injector prefilled with relief cream.", category = "medicine", tags = "medicine", slotRotation = -45f, destroyAtZeroCondition = false, combineable = true, scaleWeightWithCondition = true, weight = 0.25f, value = 8, rec = new Recognition(5), Syringe = new SyringeProperties { Capacity = 100f, AmountPerFullUse = 100f, AutoFill = false, // Not sure what this is? Read the next page for liquid documentation. DefaultContents = { new LiquidStack("reliefcream", 100f) } }, SpawnFrequency = 1 }, AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.reliefinjector.png") ); The liquid decides what injection actually does. WaterContainerItem.Inject drains the liquid stack and calls onInject when that liquid is injectable, falling back to onHealthUse for older registrations. You'll learn more about liquids and their use on the Liquids page. Containers Containers are runtime components, not just item stats. CUCoreLib's container module adds or configures a vanilla Container component when the item starts. Capacity maps to the container's maximum held weight. MaxWeightPerItem limits individual items. EncumbranceReduction maps to the vanilla encumbrance multiplier: 1f means normal weight, 0.5f means the contents feel half as heavy. ItemRegistry.Register( "cinderstalkbag", new CustomItemInfo { fullName = "Cinderstalk Bag", description = "A compact all-natural bag. Who says plants can't be stylish?", category = "custom", weight = 1.2f, value = 18, tags = "cangetwet", rec = new Recognition(6), Container = new ContainerProperties { Capacity = 5f, MaxWeightPerItem = 2f, EncumbranceReduction = 0.65f }, SpawnFrequency = 1 }, AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.cinderstalk-bag.png") ); Battery-powered items Battery-powered tools use the vanilla BatteryItem component. CUCoreLib's battery module adds one, chooses the vanilla battery size from Preset , and uses StartCharge only for the initial fill amount. Use values from 0f to 1f when you want a percentage of the preset size, or values above 1f when you want an absolute charge amount. Use this when the item itself stores charge or accepts battery behavior; use vanilla BatteryInfo when you are registering an actual battery item. Battery items automatically gain BatteryDecay , so you usually just set decayMinutes to control how quickly charge drains. ItemRegistry.Register( "portablelamp", new CustomItemInfo { fullName = "Portable lamp", description = "A battery-fed lamp for the fuzzy cave explorer.", category = "utility", tags = "belttool", usable = true, value = 22, weight = 0.8f, rec = new Recognition(5), decayMinutes = 180f, Battery = new BatteryProperties { StartCharge = 35f, Preset = BatteryItem.BatteryPreset.Medium }, Light = new LightProperties { Intensity = 0.75f, Color = Color.white, FalloffIntensity = 0.5f, PointLightOuterRadius = 7.5f, PointLightInnerRadius = 0f, PointLightOuterAngle = 360f, PointLightInnerAngle = 360f, LightType = CustomLightType.Point, Rotation = 0f, Offset = Vector2.zero }, SpawnFrequency = 1 }, AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.portablelamp.png") ); Non-gun weapons For melee tools and small weapons, ToolProperties builds a vanilla AttackInfo and calls Body.Attack . This gives custom tools the same swing, raycast, hit sound, cooldown, damage-number, and block-damage path used by vanilla tools. ItemRegistry.Register("glassshiv", new CustomItemInfo { fullName = "Glass shiv", description = "A sharpened piece of glass wrapped in cloth.", category = "weapon", tags = "tool,cangetwet,cutting", weight = 0.25f, value = 4, rec = new Recognition(3), Tool = new ToolProperties { Damage = 22f, StructuralDamage = 8f, AttackCooldownMultiplier = 0.7f, Distance = 4.6f, KnockBack = 120f, Cooldown = 0.28f, StaminaUse = 0.35f, Piercing = true, ConditionLossOnHit = 0.08f } }, AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.glassshiv.png"), 1); Equippables Wearables are regular items with wearable fields set. wearSlotId is the save/load and replacement key. desiredWearLimb points the primary visual/armor behavior at a body region, while wearableArmor and wearableIsolation affect protection and temperature. Use VisualOffset when you want the held hand sprite moved without changing the worn sprite, use MultiWornSprites when the same wearable should also draw extra pieces on other limbs, and set WearableSortingOrder when you need that whole wearable stack to use a higher or lower draw priority than other equipment. If a wearable needs a custom script, use the same item-side AddSpawnComponent<T>() helper described below. There is no separate wearable-only script hook. ItemRegistry.Register( "fieldpack", new CustomItemInfo { fullName = "Field Pack", description = "A versatile pack for carrying supplies.", category = "tool", wearable = true, wearableCanBeHeld = true, desiredWearLimb = "UpTorso", wearSlotId = "back", wearableArmor = 0.18f, wearableIsolation = 0.08f, wearableHitDurabilityLossMultiplier = 0.7f, weight = 1.1f, value = 14, tags = "cangetwet", rec = new Recognition(4), WornSprite = AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.fieldpack-worn.png"), WornSpriteOffset = new Vector2(0f, -0.04f), VisualOffset = new Vector2(0f, -0.02f), WearableSortingOrder = 206, MultiWornSprites = new Dictionary { ["DownTorso"] = AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.fieldpack-bedroll.png"), ["HandB"] = AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.fieldpack-strap.png") }, Container = new ContainerProperties { Capacity = 8f, MaxWeightPerItem = 3f, EncumbranceReduction = 0.5f }, SpawnFrequency = 1 } .SetMultiWornSpriteOffset(new Vector2(0f, -0.02f), AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.fieldpack-bedroll.png")) .SetMultiWornSpriteOffset("HandB", new Vector2(-0.01f, 0.01f)), AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.fieldpack.png") ); In this example, we combined the container tag, a primary WornSprite , and two MultiWornSprites entries to make one backpack draw across multiple limbs while still behaving like a normal wearable container. A lot of more unique items such as this can be made with combinations of tags. Give it a try! Targeting specific loot sources Leave DropPool unset when the item should follow its broad category like vanilla. Set DropPool when the item should target explicit sources instead, such as corpses, one crate type, trader species, or capsules. ItemRegistry.Register( "fieldbandagekit", new CustomItemInfo { fullName = "Field bandage kit", description = "A compact med kit meant for emergency caches and corpses.", category = "medical", tags = "medicine,dressing,cangetwet", weight = 0.25f, value = 12, DropPool = DropPool.Corpse | DropPool.MedicalCrate | DropPool.AllTraders, SpawnFrequency = 2, WorldSpawnPerChunk = 0.02f }, AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.fieldbandagekit.png") ); In that example, the item no longer relies on category fallback for pooled sources. It instead uses the explicit DropPool flags, while direct loose worldgen counts come from WorldSpawnPerChunk . Decay bit flags decayInfo is a byte, but it represents bit flags from ItemInfo.DecayType . Combine flags with bitwise OR (|). The enums are: NoDecayWithoutContainerItem (1) , NoDecayWhenNotWorn (2) , NoDecayWhenStill (4) , and BatteryDecay (16) . decayMinutes = 240f, decayInfo = (byte)( ItemInfo.DecayType.NoDecayWhenNotWorn | ItemInfo.DecayType.NoDecayWhenStill ); BatteryDecay (16) changes decay from normal item condition loss into battery drain. Use it for battery-powered items that should consume charge over time instead of rotting or breaking down normally. Note: The item still needs decayMinutes for decay speed. SpawnComponents type names !! Legacy !! Prefer custom item scripts, in the next page. For plugin-authored item scripts, AddSpawnComponent<T>() exists. It stores the runtime-resolvable assembly-qualified name for you, so you do not have to hand-write Type.GetType(...) strings. ItemRegistry.Register( "ToggleBlade", new CustomItemInfo { fullName = "Toggle blade", category = "weapon" } .AddSpawnComponent<ToggleBladeScript>(), icon ); SpawnComponents remains the backing list, so you can still fill it manually for uncommon reflection-driven cases. When you do, use the full type name plus the assembly name without the .dll extension. Example: "TestModd.ToggleBladeScript, TestModd" . Custom data CustomData is for your own mod's item-side custom state defaults: tuning values, upgrade tiers, internal labels, or small constants you want to keep near the registration. CUCoreLib copies those values onto each spawned item instance so one item can change without rewriting every other item of the same type. ItemRegistry.Register( "laserdrill", new CustomItemInfo { fullName = "Laser drill", category = "tool", CustomData = { ["beamRange"] = 8f, ["warmupSeconds"] = 0.35f, ["upgradeFamily"] = "laserdrill" } }, AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedSprite("Images.laserdrill.png") ); Retrieve it from the item with ItemRegistry.GetCustomData . The generic type is intentional: the dictionary stores object , so callers should ask for the type they expect. float beamRange = ItemRegistry.GetCustomData(item, "beamRange", 4f); Logger.LogInfo($"Laser drill range: {beamRange}"); Consider adding a function to encapsulate the retrieval logic. If the data changes per spawned item, update it through ItemRegistry.SetCustomData rather than mutating the shared registered definition. Tile CustomData still remains registration metadata.
